title: What's happening?
subtitle: Pick the closest match — we'll walk it through.

branches.label: Device doesn't connect (the computer doesn't see it)

node.title: Does the device show up in your operating system's MIDI list?
node.subtitle: Mac: Audio MIDI Setup. Windows: Device Manager → Sound, video, game controllers.

yes.title: Check the browser's MIDI connection.
fix: Open the page in Chrome (Brave and Edge work too): play.playtronica.com for Playtron, synth.playtronica.com for the other devices. Safari and Firefox don't speak MIDI.
Connect the device first, then open or reload the browser tab.
If you accidentally clicked Block on the MIDI permission popup, go to the browser's Site Settings → MIDI → set play.playtronica.com or synth.playtronica.com to Allow.
yes.stuck: Send a short video showing: the device, your browser address bar, and the MIDI permission popup if it appears.

no.title: Check the data cable, port and OS MIDI list.
fix: Try a different USB data cable and port. Check that any required adapter carries data.
Compare a direct USB connection. On Mac, use the connection checks below to compare a data hub you already have.
On Mac, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → check if any prompt is asking permission for the device.
no.stuck: Send the cable model + the port you're using + a screenshot of your OS's MIDI list (Mac: Audio MIDI Setup; Windows: Device Manager).

node.title: Are you in Chrome, Brave, or Edge?
node.subtitle: About 40% of 'no sound' cases resolve at this step.

yes.title: Did you click Allow on the MIDI permission popup?

node.title: Are you grounded — bare skin on a gold corner of the device?

yes.title: Does the LED blink when you touch a clipped object?
Check MIDI reception and sound settings.
fix: Open Play at play.playtronica.com. Press No sound? Check & report at the bottom of Play.
Still silent in Play? Try a web synth at synth.playtronica.com (Dots Piano is a reliable starting point).
Refresh the Play or synth tab — sometimes the page loses the MIDI connection after a few minutes.
If you're using a DAW, make sure a track is armed to receive MIDI and the volume isn't muted.

links.label: Playtron — if Playtron is not playing

no.title: Check the contact at the object end.
fix: Wet the object slightly — a damp finger across the surface usually helps.
Move the alligator clip to a different spot on the object — more contact area = stronger signal.
Try a known-good object (a banana, a piece of citrus) and compare the response with your original setup.

no.title: Grounding is the most common 'no sound' cause on Playtron.
fix: Put your bare hand on a gold corner of Playtron — the two gold corners are the ground, and either one works. Bare skin, not over clothing.
Or, for more freedom, clip a ground cable to a gold corner and hold the other end in your hand — the ground has to touch your skin, not a radiator or a laptop.
Test again with a fresh object.

node.title: Does a MIDI monitor receive events from Biotron?
node.subtitle: Record the event type and MIDI channel. LED behaviour alone does not confirm MIDI reception.

yes.title: Check the MIDI channel and synth input.
fix: Check that the synth listens to the MIDI channel reported by the monitor.
For plant input on Channel 1 only, check that each contact is on a different branch or leaf, at least 2 cm apart.
For plant input on Channel 1 only, check whether the plant needs watering. Channel 2 events alone do not establish a plant-contact problem.

no.title: No MIDI events received — check the connection.
fix: Unplug and reconnect once. Recheck the MIDI monitor and OS MIDI list.
Before firmware recovery, identify your device and board revision using the recovery guide below.
If the revision is unknown or not covered by the guide, stop and email support with clear photos of both sides.

links.label: Firmware recovery — identify device and revision first

node.title: Are you holding both gold pads with bare skin?

yes.title: Check synth MIDI reception.
fix: Try a different synth — Dots Piano is reliable.
Confirm the synth shows TouchMe in its MIDI device list.
Test with a MIDI monitor (MorningStar online) to see if TouchMe is sending notes regardless of the synth.

no.title: TouchMe needs both ends gripped to complete the circuit.
fix: Hold it like a remote control — one hand on each conductive pad.
Bare skin, not through a sleeve.
If you're sharing with a friend, both of you grip one end and touch each other — that also completes the circuit.

yes.title: Check whether the receiver gets Orbita MIDI.
fix: Orbita doesn't make sound on its own. You need a synth or DAW receiving its MIDI.
In your DAW, set Orbita as a MIDI input and arm a track to receive.
Make sure the receiving track has a sound on it (instrument plugin or sample).

no.title: Check Orbita's cable and USB connection.
fix: Try a different USB cable and port.
Before considering recovery, identify the device and board revision in the guide below. If unknown or unsupported, email support.

links.label: Firmware recovery — identify device and revision first

no.title: Check MIDI permissions.
fix: Open your browser's settings → Site Settings → MIDI.
Find play.playtronica.com or synth.playtronica.com in the list.
Set it to Allow.
Reload the page. The permission popup may reappear — click Allow.

no.title: Switch to Chrome, Brave, or Edge.
fix: Web MIDI is only supported in Chromium-based browsers — Chrome, Brave, Edge.
Open play.playtronica.com (Playtron) or synth.playtronica.com in one of those.
Connect the device first, then open the browser tab.

branches.label: Strange behaviour — random notes, wrong note per pin, weird timing

node.title: Do notes fire even when you don't touch the plant?

yes.title: Check which MIDI events are being received.
fix: Record the unexpected events and their channels in a MIDI monitor.
Compare the MIDI activity with the light sensor uncovered and covered.
Record the events and current settings for support before changing settings or firmware.

no.title: Review the symptoms before considering recovery.
fix: Identify the device and board revision using the recovery guide below before any firmware recovery.
If the revision is unknown or not covered by the guide, stop and email support with clear photos of both sides.

links.label: Firmware recovery — identify device and revision first

node.title: Does a specific pin send a wrong note?

yes.title: Check the current Playtron mapping.
fix: Open settings.playtronica.com/#/playtron in Chrome.
Pick a preset (e.g. Major C) and click Send.
Or, in Custom mode, manually re-map each pin.

no.title: Try a fresh ground and a fresh object.
fix: Re-ground yourself (bare skin on a gold corner).
Replace your test object with a known-good one (a banana).
If only certain pins act up, the alligator clips on those pins may be making poor contact — try wiggling them or swapping clips.

node.title: Identify the device and revision before recovery.
fix: Record the behaviour and what your computer or MIDI app detects.
Use the recovery guide below to identify the device and board revision first.
If the revision is unknown or unsupported, stop and email support with clear photos of both sides.
If the behaviour persists, email support with a video and the steps already tried. A reset result alone does not establish a hardware fault.

links.label: Firmware recovery — identify device and revision first

branches.label: Physical damage — USB connector loose, pin corroded, board cracked

node.title: Send us a photo — we'll sort it.
fix: Take a clear photo of the damage in good light.
Email support@playtronica.com with subject 'Defective #[your order number]'.
Include: photo, brief description, and your order number if you have it.
For corrosion on Playtron pins specifically, see the Playtron FAQ — light corrosion is fixable at home.

branches.label: Something else — describe in an email

node.title: Email us with as much detail as you can.
fix: Send a 30–60 second video showing the device, your screen, and what's not working.
Include: which device, your OS and browser, what you've already tried.
Email support@playtronica.com with subject 'Issue — [one-line description]'.
We reply in 1–3 business days.
